findings.evidence: `rg` shows line 53 has `(U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n)`, while line 86 already proves the a.e. variable-jet form `{U V : α → ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n}`; Mathlib has `Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable`, `StronglyMeasurable.prodMk`, and `stronglyMeasurable_const`.
findings.fix: Add `stronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand_apply₂` with assumptions `hU hV : StronglyMeasurable ...`, prove it by composing the same continuous evaluation map used in `aestronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand_apply₂`, and derive the fixed-jet lemma from it using `stronglyMeasurable_const`.
findings.issue: `stronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand_apply` only handles fixed `U V`, even though the natural strong analogue of line 86 is for strongly measurable jet fields `U V : α → ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n`.

summary: The coefficient-field measurability lemmas are at the right level, but the strong scalar evaluation API is left at a fixed-jet special case while the a.e. API proves the natural variable-jet theorem.
